top_story.headline: Air Force picks an individual airshow announcer, with no federal contract on record, as the sole source for Dover's 2027 air boss job
top_story.dek: The Dover Air Force Base open house would pay a named person, not a company, to run its air boss, narration and sound operations with no competition.
paragraphs: The Department of the Air Force plans to award a contract without competition to William David Schultz for air boss, narration, sound and ground-support services at the 2027 First State Airshow at Dover Air Force Base in Delaware. The notice, titled “Intent to Award Sole Source - Air Boss,” was posted as a Special Notice on October 15 rather than in the Justification category. No value is stated.

The draft performance work statement sets the show for June 12-13, 2027. The air boss would direct performers, liaise with the Federal Aviation Administration and air traffic control, manage taxiing aircraft and vehicle traffic, and run the mandatory pilot safety briefing. A narrator would prepare introductions and record announcements for financial sponsors. The audio requirement calls for speakers along a 5,000-foot crowd line, sound projection to crowds of at least 50,000, and a control platform of at least 320 square feet.

The notice’s stated reason for skipping competition is that he is the only qualified source. As extracted from the notice, it cites more than 200 hours of warbird airshow experience, operations alongside the Thunderbirds, Blue Angels and Snowbirds, and the specialized FAA and military requirements. USAspending shows no federal contract on record under this name since fiscal 2008, so this would be the first on record. The performance work statement attached to the notice is marked as a draft.

sections.headline: Defense Logistics Agency justified a Jordan jet fuel deal only after awarding it, citing a Middle East fuel crisis
paragraphs: There are 52 new sole-source justifications today, 20 of them posted under other notice types such as Special Notices and Award Notices, and none repeat earlier editions. Twelve that mainly keep an incumbent running are in Extensions, and the Air Force airshow notice is the Top Story. Most of the remainder are routine parts, licenses and maintenance.

blocks.text: Must read

blocks.title: Defense Logistics Agency justifies after the fact a sole-source jet fuel deal for Jordan, citing a Middle East fuel crisis
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
blocks.text: The justification covers a modification to contract SPE60525D9504 for 34.3 million gallons of aviation turbine fuel for Jordan posts, camps and stations, after an urgent request from a Middle East team on March 4, 2026. The scanned document, which is partly garbled, says it was approved and publicized after the award, and the stated cause is an “unpredictable regional fuel crisis in the Middle East area of operations.” It says no market research was done because of time sensitivity, and the rationale names the incumbent contractor.

blocks.title: Navy buys urgent Aerosonde drone changes from Textron without competition after the contract’s authority lapsed
meta: only one company can do it
blocks.text: The class justification authorizes three sole-source modifications to task orders under basic ordering agreement N0001921G0008. They move shipboard Aerosonde support for an urgent Africa Command requirement, reinstate terminated operational line items and relocate them to new classified Central Command sites after an operational halt directive, and add a directed change for a mine countermeasures sensor. The document says the parent justification “expired in March 2026,” which is why this one was needed, and that Textron is the sole original maker and holds the proprietary data. It was posted as an Award Notice that lists $2,800,695 awarded September 30.

blocks.title: NASA buys a used, modified Ford F-59 from Enterprise Rent-A-Car for its Artemis closeout crew without competition
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
National Aeronautics and Space Administration, Kennedy Space Center
blocks.text: The vehicle is already modified and configured for the Exploration Ground Systems Closeout Crew, and the agency says there is no time to acquire and modify another before it is needed. The justification cites Executive Order 14369, “Ensuring American Space Superiority,” and says it advances a return to the lunar surface no later than 2028. The document states the cost is “approximately $70,000.”

blocks.title: Navy gave Kapule a Japan landslide cleanup contract before posting its sole-source justification
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command Far East
blocks.text: A July 6, 2026 landslide at Commander Fleet Activities Sasebo left a boulder and unstable slope. The justification says the Navy first expected Seabees to do the work, learned on August 19 they lacked the equipment, sent Kapule a request for proposals August 27, and awarded the contract September 18, before the justification was posted. It says competing the job would add at least two to four months and that Kapule was already on base for construction projects.

blocks.title: Army gives Vectrus an urgent, uncompeted modification to inventory equipment sets in Kuwait
meta: skipped the competition among existing contract holders
blocks.text: The modification to a LOGCAP task order covers a rapid inventory and technical inspection of equipment staged in Kuwait in support of Operation Spartan Shield. The justification says Vectrus “was the only contractor to receive a LOGCAP V task order” in the Southwest Asia region of U.S. Central Command, and that any other contractor would need months to onboard.

sections.headline: National Institutes of Health extends an epidemiology contract two years, blaming the Department of Government Efficiency order for recompete delays
paragraphs: There are 12 new extensions or bridges that mainly keep an incumbent running. Three cards follow, then the rest in a list.

blocks.title: National Institutes of Health extends Social & Scientific Systems’ epidemiology contract two years and adds $20 million without competition, citing delays blamed on the Department of Government Efficiency order
meta: only one company can do it
National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences
blocks.text: The ordering period on contract HHSN273201600003I was set to end June 29, 2026 and would now run through June 29, 2028. The ceiling would rise from $112 million to $132 million. The justification says recompete planning began in 2025, but Executive Order 14158, which established the “Department of Government Efficiency,” “caused unforeseen circumstances” that delayed the acquisition, citing staffing changes and internal realignments. It also cites more than three decades of the incumbent’s work for the institute.

blocks.title: Federal Law Enforcement Training Center bridges its roleplayer contract with the incumbent while a Government Accountability Office protest freezes the follow-on
meta: only one company can do it
blocks.text: The justification says the follow-on contract 70LGLY26CGLB00006 “is currently under a statutory stay of performance due to a bid protest filed with the Government Accountability Office.” It calls the incumbent “the only realistic option” and says a lapse would put training at the Glynco, Georgia center at risk. The training serves about 100 federal agencies, according to the justification.

blocks.title: Air Force extends Peraton’s nuclear planning system contract and raises its ceiling without competition
meta: only one company can do it
blocks.text: The justification approves a modification to task order FA873022F8506 that extends the period of performance and raises the ceiling for maintaining two legacy planning applications and building their replacements for U.S. Strategic Command. The document describes the planning system as “the nation’s only comprehensive system for developing Level 4 nuclear plans and options for the President.” The contracting officer’s signature is dated September 23, 2026.

sections.headline: Air Force Test Center opens a ‘multi-billion dollar’ consortium for test infrastructure projects at Arnold Engineering Development Complex
paragraphs: There are 293 new solicitations, 57 flagged. Two cards and a list follow. Late document findings on earlier notices are included.

blocks.title: Air Force asks for white papers to form the AEDC Velocity Alliance, a consortium for a multi-billion dollar run of test facility projects
meta: Air Force Test Center and Arnold Engineering Development Complex
blocks.text: The notice says the consortium is established under 10 U.S.C. 4022 other-transaction authority to modernize national test infrastructure. Once established, all projects under it “will be competed exclusively among Alliance members.” The notice has 44 attachments, none read yet.

blocks.title: Navy solicits a Marine Raider facilities complex at Camp Lejeune as bidders raise shielding and drawing-access questions
meta: Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command Mid-Atlantic
blocks.text: The design-bid-build project at Stone Bay covers Marine Special Operations battalion operations, supply, communications and intelligence space plus company headquarters and team facilities. The funding clause in amendment 0005 allots $79.5 million on execution and a $71.4 million fiscal 2027 increment. A responses document says a radio-frequency shielded space that passes all IEEE 299 tables on six sides is “extremely expensive… (if not impossible).” It also says the security plan requiring U.S. citizens “will be modified to allow US persons.” An offeror comment in another responses document says classified-adjacent drawings were released publicly and later pulled behind a non-disclosure agreement. Most of these files were posted between June and October 1.

sections.headline: Delayed Pentagon data shows $23.5 million for Booz Allen to support a U.S. Air Force security team at Pakistani air bases
paragraphs: USAspending shows 140 new awards of $2 million or more today, 118 of them Defense Department awards published after the 90-day hold. It also shows 11 large modifications and 11 cuts. The 128 routine ones are listed, each linked, in “USAspending: Every Other New Award” at the end of the edition. One $2 million-plus award worth $2.1 million cites Executive Order 14398. No White House or Executive Office of the President awards turned up.

Booz Allen Hamilton Inc. received $23,535,656 from the Department of the Air Force for support services at Pakistan Air Force bases Shahbaz and Mushaf for the U.S. Air Force technical security team and designated representatives. footer.known_gaps: No source errors were reported. OMB Apportionments reported no new apportionment files for October 11-16. Of 2,204 attachments on 496 SAM.gov notices, 89 are access-restricted on SAM.gov and 1,681 were queued unread; 1,785 files in all are queued and will be read over the next editions, with any findings returning as late document findings. More than 1,000 links to outside portals (mostly DIBBS and NECO) were not followed. Several justification values were unverified and are not stated.
